title: Is π Equal to 180? Radians Explained Simply | PUC Maths Class 11
description:
Half a turn of a bicycle wheel is 180 degrees, and it is also π radians. So when Aarav's cycling app says his wheel turned 3 radians, is that more or less than half a turn? In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Maths (NCERT Chapter 3, Trigonometric Functions) we learn to switch between degrees and radians with one fact and two rules.

You will watch one turn measured on two rulers at once, degrees on the outside and radians on the inside, then see about 57 degree slices fill one radian. We derive 1 radian = 180°/π and 1° = π/180 radian step by step, build the table of common angles, separate π the number from π radians the angle, convert 22° 30′ in a worked example, fix the trap of using the wrong factor, and solve an original JEE Main pattern clock question. Two pause-and-think questions, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11 and JEE Main students.
